relations.definition: To guide or direct someone or something.
relations.embedding_query_text: led: To guide or direct someone or something.

chosen_property.label: director
chosen_property.justification: Best match among candidates for the given instances.

candidates.label: director
candidates.comment: A creative leadership relation between a clip, creative work season, episode, event, movie, or video game and a person who directed it. Also called: directed by, filmmaker, showrunner. Examples: "Movie" director "Steven Spielberg", "TV Episode" director "Ava DuVernay", "Video Game" director "Hideo Kojima". Distinct from directors, which is a plural property for multiple directors.

candidates.label: directors
candidates.comment: A creative leadership relation between a clip, episode, movie, or video game and the persons who directed it. Also called: directed by, filmmakers, showrunners. Examples: "Movie" directors "Joel Coen, Ethan Coen", "TV Episode" directors "Various Directors", "Video Game" directors "Hideo Kojima, Yoji Shinkawa". Distinct from director, which is a singular property for a single director.

candidates.label: supply
candidates.comment: A resource relation between a how-to guide or direction and a consumable supply required for its execution. Also called "required supply", "consumable item", "material needed", "ingredient". Examples: "The recipe has supply flour", "The how-to direction requires supply glue", "This guide lists several supply items.". Distinct from tool, which refers to a non-consumable instrument.

candidates.label: toRecipient
candidates.comment: A direct recipient relation between a message and the specific audience, contact point, organization, or person it was sent to. Also called direct addressee, message recipient, primary recipient. Examples: "Email toRecipient 'john.doe@example.com'", "Message toRecipient 'Marketing Department'", "SMS toRecipient 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from recipient, which is a more general property for any recipient.

candidates.label: duringMedia
candidates.comment: A during media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL representing the circumstances while performing this direction. Also called "instructional media", "step-by-step video", "visual guide". Examples: "How-to direction 'Attach part A' duringMedia 'Video of assembly'", "Direction 'Stir mixture' duringMedia 'Image of stirring technique'".

candidates.label: step
candidates.comment: A component relation between a how-to guide and a single instruction, section, or creative work that forms part of the process. Also called "instructional step", "how-to instruction", "process step", "guide step". Examples: "The recipe has step 'Chop vegetables'", "The guide's step is a video tutorial", "This how-to includes a step for assembly.". Distinct from steps, which refers to a collection of steps.

candidates.label: coach
candidates.comment: A leadership relation between a sports team and the person who acts as its coach. Also called "team coach", "trainer", "manager". Examples: "Basketball team coach John Smith", "Soccer team coach Jane Doe".

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: sender
candidates.comment: The audience, organization, or person initiating and transmitting a message or action. Also called originator, dispatcher, message source, sender of message. Examples: `Email Message` sender `John Doe`, `ReceiveAction` sender `Customer Service`, `Broadcast Message` sender `News Organization`. Distinct from `recipient`, which is the receiving party.

relations.embedding_query_text: found: To discover or determine something.

instances: Toddler food research -> Ultraprocessed foods are unhealthy

chosen_property.label: discoveredInStudy
chosen_property.definition: The relation between a research study and a statement that was found or determined through the study.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the observed signature and instances.

candidates.label: identifyingTest
candidates.comment: An identifying test relation between a medical sign and a medical test that can detect it. Also called diagnostic test, detection test, test for sign. Examples: "A medical sign has an identifying test of a blood panel.", "The symptom is detected by an identifying test.", "This sign requires an identifying test.". Distinct from identifyingExam, which refers to a physical examination.

candidates.label: name
candidates.comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: signDetected
candidates.comment: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Examples: `Blood Test` signDetected `MedicalSign: Elevated White Blood Cell Count`, `X-Ray` signDetected `MedicalSign: Bone Fracture`, `Physical Exam` signDetected `MedicalSign: Swelling`. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: geoCoveredBy
candidates.comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

relations.embedding_query_text: stated: To express or declare something.

instances: Jane Houlihan -> Ultraprocessed foods are unhealthy

chosen_property.label: interpretedAsClaim
chosen_property.justification: Best match among candidates for expressing a statement made by a person.

candidates.label: copyrightNotice
candidates.comment: A textual declaration relation between a creative work and the statement describing its copyright aspects. Also called: copyright statement, copyright declaration, copyright text. Examples: "My Novel" copyright notice "© 2023 John Doe", "Company Website" copyright notice "Copyright 2023 Example Corp. All Rights Reserved.", "Academic Paper" copyright notice "Published under CC BY 4.0 license". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which identifies the entity owning the copyright.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: name
candidates.comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.

candidates.label: expressedIn
candidates.comment: An expressed in relation between a gene and the anatomical structure, system, or biological entity where its activity has been experimentally observed. Also called: gene activity location, observed in, found in. Examples: "Gene A" expressed in "Brain", "Gene B" expressed in "Liver", "Gene C" expressed in "Digestive System".

candidates.label: disambiguatingDescription
candidates.comment: A clarifying description relation between a thing and a short text used to distinguish it from similar items. Also called: clarifying description, distinguishing text, unique description. Examples: "Apple" disambiguating description "The fruit, not the company.", "Mercury" disambiguating description "The planet, not the element.", "Jaguar" disambiguating description "The animal, not the car brand.". Distinct from description, which is a general description.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: legalRepresentative
candidates.comment: A legal representation relation between an organization and the person(s) authorized to act on its behalf in legal matters. Also called authorized representative, legal agent, official representative, corporate officer. Examples: An organization has a legalRepresentative of 'its CEO'. A company's legalRepresentative is 'its sole administrator'. The board appointed 'Jane Doe' as legalRepresentative. Distinct from employee, which is a general employment relation, not specifically legal representation.

candidates.label: announcementLocation
candidates.comment: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: option
candidates.comment: A text or thing representing an option available for a choose action. Also called choice, alternative, selection. Examples: "Choose Meal Action option 'Chicken'", "Choose Color Action option 'Blue'", "Choose Destination Action option 'Paris'". Distinct from object, which is the general item acted upon.

relations.definition: To give guidance or recommendation to someone.
relations.embedding_query_text: advised: To give guidance or recommendation to someone.

chosen_property.label: advisedCountry
chosen_property.definition: The relation between a person and a country they have given guidance or recommendation to.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly fits the relation of a person advising a country.

candidates.label: recommendationStrength
candidates.comment: A recommendation strength relation between a medical guideline recommendation and its categorized level of evidence or support. Also called strength of evidence, guideline strength. Examples: "A medical guideline recommendation has a recommendation strength 'Class I'.", "A treatment guideline has a recommendation strength 'Strong'.", "A diagnostic recommendation has a recommendation strength 'Grade B'."

candidates.label: guideline
candidates.comment: A guideline relation between a medical entity and a related medical guideline. Also called: related guideline, medical recommendation, clinical protocol. Examples: "Hypertension" guideline "AHA Guideline for Hypertension", "Diabetes Treatment" guideline "NICE Guideline for Diabetes", "COVID-19 Management" guideline "WHO COVID-19 Guidelines". Distinct from guidelineSubject, which is the subject of the guideline.

candidates.label: suggestedMeasurement
candidates.comment: A quantitative value representing a suggested range of body measurements for an intended audience or person, often for wearable products. Also called "size recommendation", "body measurement range", "fit guide", "sizing suggestion". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedMeasurement inseam 32-34 inches", "The size specification includes suggestedMeasurement height 170-190 cm", "This product is designed for a suggestedMeasurement chest 40-42 inches."

candidates.label: foodWarning
candidates.comment: A food warning relation between a drug and any precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding food consumption while taking it. Also called: dietary restrictions, food interactions, consumption advice. Examples: "Warfarin" food warning "Avoid grapefruit, limit Vitamin K rich foods", "Antibiotics" food warning "Do not take with dairy products", "MAOIs" food warning "Avoid aged cheeses and cured meats".

candidates.label: expertConsiderations
candidates.comment: An expert considerations relation between a diet and the medical expert advice pertinent to that dietary plan. Also called: medical advice, professional guidance, health warnings. Examples: "Keto Diet" expert considerations "Consult a doctor if you have kidney issues", "Vegan Diet" expert considerations "Ensure adequate B12 supplementation", "Low-Sodium Diet" expert considerations "Monitor blood pressure regularly".

candidates.label: guidelineDate
candidates.comment: A guideline date relation between a medical guideline and the date its recommendations were issued. Also called: recommendation date, issue date, publication date. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" guideline date "2017-11-13", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" guideline date "2020-08-19", "WHO COVID-19 Guidelines" guideline date "2023-03-01".

candidates.label: suggestedGender
candidates.comment: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."

candidates.label: pregnancyWarning
candidates.comment: A medical attribute providing precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding a drug's use during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy precautions, drug-pregnancy risks, maternal warnings. Examples: A drug has a pregnancy warning 'Consult doctor before use'. The medication includes a pregnancy warning about 'potential fetal harm'. There is a pregnancy warning against 'use in first trimester'.

candidates.label: recommendedIntake
candidates.comment: A recommended intake relation between a dietary supplement and the suggested dosage schedule for a specific population. Also called suggested dosage, dosage instructions, intake guidelines. Examples: "A vitamin supplement has a recommended intake '1 tablet daily for adults'.", "A mineral supplement has a recommended intake '2 capsules twice a day'.", "A protein powder has a recommended intake '30g post-workout'."

candidates.label: warning
candidates.comment: A warning relation between a drug and any FDA or other safety advisories. Also called drug warning, safety advisory, health alert. Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".

candidates.label: suggestedAge

candidates.label: suggestedMinAge

Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMinAge, which specifies only the minimum.

candidates.label: potentialAction

Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: possibleTreatment
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a potential treatment, drug, or therapy to address a medical condition, sign, or symptom. Also called potential therapy, recommended treatment, intervention option. Examples: A medical condition has a possible treatment of 'antibiotics'. A symptom has a possible treatment of 'pain relievers'. Hypertension has a possible treatment of 'lifestyle modification'.

candidates.label: recommendedIntake

candidates.label: potentialUse

candidates.label: worksFor

Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: practicesAt

Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by, is a doctor at. Examples: Dr. Smith practices at 'General Hospital'. Dr. Jones practices at 'City Clinic'. candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: workLocation

Also called employment location, office address, workplace. Examples: John workLocation MainOffice, Jane workLocation RemoteHome, CompanyEmployee workLocation BranchOffice. candidates.label: workFeatured

Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. candidates.label: workPerformed

Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: exampleOfWork

Examples: "Mona Lisa (print)" example of work "Mona Lisa (original painting)", "Hamlet (film)" example of work "Hamlet (play)", "Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)" example of work "Star Wars: A New Hope (film)".

candidates.label: translationOfWork

candidates.label: workHours

candidates.label: encodesCreativeWork

candidates.label: quarantineGuidelines
candidates.comment: A quarantine guidelines relation between a special announcement and information regarding quarantine rules. Also called isolation rules, self-quarantine instructions. Examples: "A special announcement provides quarantine guidelines for travelers.", "A public health update includes quarantine guidelines for close contacts.", "A government notice details quarantine guidelines for returning citizens."

candidates.label: recommendedIntake
candidates.comment: A recommended intake relation between a dietary supplement and the suggested dosage schedule for a specific population. Also called suggested dosage, dosage instructions, intake guidelines. Examples: "A vitamin supplement has a recommended intake '1 tablet daily for adults'.", "A mineral supplement has a recommended intake '2 capsules twice a day'.", "A protein powder has a recommended intake '30g post-workout'."

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: healthPlanCoinsuranceOption
candidates.comment: A coinsurance option relation between a health plan cost-sharing specification and a description of how coinsurance applies. Also called coinsurance rule, coinsurance terms, option for coinsurance. Examples: "Health plan cost-sharing has a coinsurance option 'after deductible'.", "The specification includes a coinsurance option.", "This plan's coinsurance option is 'before deductible'."

instances: Toddler food research -> NOVA classification system

chosen_property.label: utilizedSystem
chosen_property.definition: The relation between a research study and a classification system it used.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property directly expresses the use of a classification system in a research study.

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

candidates.label: usesDevice
candidates.comment: A uses device relation between a medical test and the medical device employed to perform it. Also called device used, equipment for test, test instrument. Examples: "MedicalTest 'Ultrasound' usesDevice 'Ultrasound Scanner'", "MedicalTest 'ECG' usesDevice 'Electrocardiograph'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Pressure Measurement' usesDevice 'Sphygmomanometer'".

candidates.label: recipe
candidates.comment: A recipe relation between a cook action and the specific recipe used as an instrument. Also called recipe used, instructions for, cooking guide. Examples: "A cook action uses the recipe 'Classic Lasagna'.", "Baking a cake uses the recipe 'Chocolate Fudge Cake'.", "Preparing dinner uses the recipe 'Chicken Stir-fry'."

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: educationalUse
candidates.comment: An educational use relation between a creative work or learning resource and its purpose in an educational context. Also called "learning purpose", "pedagogical use", "instructional application". Examples: "Worksheet educationalUse 'Assignment'", "Video educationalUse 'Group work'", "Simulation educationalUse 'Experiment'".

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: usageInfo
candidates.comment: A usage info relation between a creative work and additional information about its use, including licensing options, citation conventions, or purchasing details. Also called usage guidelines, licensing information, rights information. Examples: "CreativeWork usageInfo 'https://example.com/usage-policy'", "Image usageInfo 'Commercial licenses available upon request.'", "Dataset usageInfo 'https://example.com/data-license'". Distinct from license, which indicates the specific license(s) applicable to the content.

candidates.label: availableLanguage
candidates.comment: A language that can be used with or at an item, service, or place. Also called: supported language, language option, communication language. Examples: "ContactPoint 'Support' availableLanguage 'en'", "Course 'Programming' availableLanguage 'es'", "LodgingBusiness 'Hotel' availableLanguage 'fr'". Distinct from inLanguage, which specifies the language of the content itself.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

chosen_property.label: studyLocation
chosen_property.justification: Best fit for the location where a research study was conducted.

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: course
candidates.comment: A location relation between an exercise action and the course where it was performed. Also called: exercise location, training course, activity venue. Examples: "Morning Run" course "Central Park Loop", "Golf Game" course "Augusta National", "Cycling Race" course "Tour de France Route".

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: broadcastOfEvent
candidates.comment: An event that is being broadcast by a broadcast event. Also called: televised event, event broadcast. Examples: "BroadcastEvent 'Super Bowl Live' broadcastOfEvent 'Super Bowl LVIII'", "BroadcastEvent 'Concert Stream' broadcastOfEvent 'Live Music Concert'."

candidates.label: howPerformed
candidates.comment: A performance method relation between a medical procedure and a description of how it is carried out. Also called procedure steps, method of procedure, execution details. Examples: "A medical procedure has a description of how it is performed.", "The surgery details how it is performed.", "This procedure outlines how it is performed."

candidates.label: exerciseCourse
candidates.comment: An exercise course relation between an exercise action and the specific place or course where the action was performed. Also called: workout location, training venue, activity course. Examples: "Morning Run" exercise course "Central Park Loop", "Swimming Practice" exercise course "Olympic Pool Lane 3", "Cycling Race" exercise course "Mountain Bike Trail". Distinct from fromLocation, which is the original location before the action.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

chosen_property.label: containedIn
chosen_property.justification: Expresses the spatial containment relation between a city and a state.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".

candidates.label: homeLocation
candidates.comment: A home location relation between a person and their residential contact point or place. Also called residence, dwelling, home address. Examples: "A person has a home location in London.", "Her home location is a specific address.", "The individual's home location is a contact point."

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: applicantLocationRequirements
candidates.comment: An applicant location requirements relation between a job posting and the administrative area(s) from which candidates can apply, especially for remote positions. Also called remote work location, eligible application region, telecommuting area. Examples: "A job posting's applicant location requirements include 'Anywhere in the US'.", "The remote job's applicant location requirements are 'Europe'."

candidates.label: bodyLocation
candidates.comment: A textual description of the location in the body of an anatomical structure or for a medical procedure. Also called: anatomical site, body region, procedure location. Examples: "AnatomicalStructure 'Heart' bodyLocation 'Chest'", "MedicalProcedure 'Appendectomy' bodyLocation 'Abdomen'."
